fixture.prompt: /new-task we want a new `autosearch co-change <path>` command. auto-etl indexes git history into parquet (commits, commit_files), but auto-search has nothing that reads it. Given a file, return the other files that historically change with it — temporal coupling, a proxy for architectural coupling that import-graph analysis misses. It's an onboarding heuristic and a refactor-safety signal. Create the requirements and explain why this matters.

human_turns: For the scoring: make the primary score directional confidence weighted by lift — score = confidence(A->B) * log(1 + lift) — with a per-commit large-commit size penalty and exponential time decay (tau = 90 days). Exclude candidates with fewer than 3 co-commits, drop commits touching more than 50 files, and if the input file has fewer than 5 commits of history return a metadata-only 'insufficient history' payload. For anything else still open, go with your recommended answer.

Engine decision: run in-process with no external dependency — read the parquet via parquet-go and aggregate in an ephemeral in-memory pure-Go SQLite (modernc.org/sqlite), scoring in Go. auto-search must stay a self-contained pure-Go binary; this supersedes any duckdb-CLI approach. For open questions, go with your recommendations.
